items.text: Pro keys. Settings › Pro key takes a key from the studio (or a link that carries one); Pro features that are built then work, and their locks go
with Pro, save as many beats as you like, and export and import them all
▶ is the robot: tap it and it plays the scenes for you, as auto play did. Its button lights while it plays
the dice joins the robot's pill, ‹ robot › ⚄; Capture sits in the middle of the bar, with source, sound and tools to its right
Settings › Hand: left mirrors the bar around Capture
muted, the speaker reverses: a dark button, the wave in blue, the speaker white
one line weight per icon size: the panel heads, the index's section icons and the bar no longer draw the same icon heavier or lighter in different places
in Random, how often it rolls is a row of beads like Auto play's: a hand for by hand, then 2 to 60 seconds; the bead timing the next roll wears a ring that fills to it

the speaker is the master mute. Tap it and what you hear goes quiet while the sound plays on (its wave still moves); scenes and Auto play can no longer turn it back on, only you can. Hold it for the shelf, to stop or change the sound
in Auto play, Changes are checkboxes: Pattern, Style and Sound, with Scene across the top for all three. Untick Sound and the music carries on across the changes
the bead that times the next scene wears a ring that fills up to it; dim when the dice picked it, a step per beat when counting beats or bars
the dice in Every is the same dice as the Random button
Touchable sound is six icon tiles (Fader, Sweep, Pan, Wash, Tide, and Mapping with Pro); point at one, or tap it, and its sentence shows in one line at the foot
Paths wears a scholar's hat, so it reads as learning: on the cover, in the index and on the suggestions card. Walk every path and the hat becomes a ribbon
on a computer, panels no longer float, pin or drag. Each opens in its own place and closes as before, until a proper desktop system arrives: one pane on the right that holds them all
